claims.text: Standard stainless steel has a native passive oxide layer.
The durability of standard stainless steel is limited under extreme corrosive conditions.
Atomic layer deposition can produce an ultrathin Al2O3 coating on stainless steel.
The ALD-deposited Al2O3 coating is pinhole-free.
High-chloride or acidic environments can cause severe corrosion of uncoated stainless steel.
ALD forms a conformal and dense Al2O3 film that seals the stainless-steel surface.
The deposited Al2O3 film is chemically inert under the proposed exposure conditions.
The ALD Al2O3 coating acts as a diffusion or physical barrier to corrosive species.
The Al2O3 coating blocks or limits chloride-ion ingress to the stainless-steel surface.
Limiting corrosive-species ingress reduces the electrochemical reactions responsible for corrosion.
Uniform, controlled coating thickness minimizes defects that could initiate localized corrosion.
ALD-coated stainless steel will have significantly lower corrosion current density than untreated stainless steel under identical aggressive conditions.
ALD-coated stainless steel will exhibit less corrosion-related weight loss than untreated stainless steel.
ALD-coated stainless steel will develop fewer corrosion pits than untreated stainless steel.
Poor film-substrate adhesion could limit the corrosion-protection effectiveness of the coating.
Prolonged high-temperature service could degrade the coating and limit its corrosion-protection effectiveness.
ALD techniques are proven methods for producing barrier coatings.
The long-term adhesion and performance of Al2O3 on stainless steel under cyclic or strongly fluctuating environments have not been fully quantified.
